passages.note: Senate Third Reading roll call: Shope voted Y on HCR2060, a bundled border-security referendum.

passages.provision_quote: This section may only be enforced prospectively. This section does not apply retroactively and shall not be construed to apply to the conduct of any person who entered this state unlawfully from a foreign nation at any time before this section becomes enforceable.
passages.note: Article 35 criminalizes illegal entry and orders removal on conviction, but only prospectively; the same bill also bundles unrelated public-benefits-fraud, e-verify-fraud, and fentanyl-sentencing provisions into one vote.

rows.reasoning: HCR2060 bundles a felony for unlawful entry with a court-ordered return to the foreign nation on conviction (applying only prospectively, never to a person who entered before the section becomes enforceable), alongside unrelated public-benefits-document-fraud, e-verify-fraud, and fentanyl-sentencing provisions, in one up-or-down referendum vote; Shope voted Y. Because the bill is multi-subject and no statement ties his Yea specifically to the illegal-entry/removal provision rather than the other three, the vote shows direction toward enforcement but cannot separate rungs 2 through 5 on 'how far should the government go in deporting undocumented immigrants'.
